items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: I was playing with that outfit, you know, different spot jobs, yeah, with Bunk and George and them.

ctx.x: Did you ever play with Bunk? I guess not the old days.

Not the old days. I played with Bunk, yeah. And after he, George and I came back from New York. That was another thing I forgot right after the wall, I was playing with that outfit, you know, different spot jobs, yeah, with Bunk and George and them. And I made that trip that time with George to California, remember? Oh yeah. That was in 56. George went replacing Joe Boston, the drummer. Well I played up there with them and came on back.
Did you ever enjoy joining Earl Hines?

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: Then I went back there in 67 with George Lewis and them group. And we didn't play Berlin. Then we played London, England in 66.

ctx.x: So far as the rock and roll. I keep instrument to play rock and roll in case if somebody jumped me up. I keep that kind of instrument to play rock and roll. But see like this, this ain't no rock and roll instrument.

You see, let me tell them this too. You see they speak about saying music is a universal language. My first time going overseas in 1966. We had a place they called Copenhagen, Munich, Germany. Because it was working out of Frankfurt, Germany. The first night we played, the first number you played, everybody sounds looking at you in Germany. You think they're not. They're taking that music. They couldn't understand our language. And I'm from the south down here. My way of speaking, where the kicks will come out…
Especially the Dixieland jazz. It reaches so many, many people. What about keeping time? Did y'all keep good time there? Did people dance to the bands?
